reason: Pan-era overview nodes (NCERT 7 Ch 6/7/8 closing summaries spanning 700-1750, or general classification lists). Not era-specific.

nodes.label: Forest Clearing and Agriculture
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Gradual clearing of forests and extension of agriculture throughout 700-1750. Forest-dwellers migrated or became peasants. New peasant groups influenced by markets, chieftains, priests and temples.
nodes.chapter_title: Tracing Changes Through a Thousand Years

nodes.label: Classical Dance Forms
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Six recognised classical forms: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathakali (Kerala), Odissi (Odisha), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Manipuri (Manipur) and Kathak (north India). Many 'folk' forms share similar characteristics.

nodes.label: Bhakti Movement Development
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: During 700-1750, the idea of bhakti emerged - a loving personal deity reachable without priests or elaborate rituals. New deities worshipped, temples built by royalty, Brahmanas gained dominance.
nodes.chapter_title: Tracing Changes Through a Thousand Years

nodes.label: Miniature Painting Traditions
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Small paintings in watercolour on cloth or paper. Earliest on palm leaves for Jaina texts in western India. Mughal style spread to Deccan and Rajput courts (Mewar, Jodhpur, Bundi, Kota, Kishangarh). Basohli and Kangra schools in hills.
